title: Artifact boot silently drops an app's code plugins: runtimeModule carries only `functions`, so `plugins: [new XPlugin()]` never mounts (and its dependencies are not shipped)
body:
Filing gate ①: a reproducible defect and a contract violation (declared ≠ delivered).
Source: evaluation of the BrightRule app (`objectstack-ai/brightrule`, branch `feature/policy-inquiry`) on ObjectOS EE `ghcr.io/objectstack-ai/objectos-ee:18.6.0`, local stack (PostgreSQL 16 + pgvector), 2026-11-23.
Dedupe: `org:objectstack-ai runtimeModule plugins` and `org:objectstack-ai artifact plugins dropped` returned nothing on this.

## What happens

An app whose `objectstack.config.ts` lists code plugins builds fine and reports them, but none of them mount when the app is booted from its artifact. Nothing says so.

BrightRule's config:

```ts
plugins: [
  new ConnectorRestPlugin(), new ConnectorOpenApiPlugin(), new ConnectorMcpPlugin(),
  new KnowledgeServicePlugin({ sources: [policyClauseKnowledgeSource()] }), // @objectstack/service-knowledge
  new KnowledgeVectorPlugin(),   // app code: OpenAI-compatible embedder + pgvector store (uses `pg`)
  new PolicyQaPlugin(),          // app code: indexes clauses at kernel:ready
],
```

1. `os build` (18.6.0) prints `Runtime: 6 plugins` and writes `dist/objectstack.json` plus `dist/objectstack-runtime.<hash>.mjs`.
2. The runtime module exports only `functions` and `meta` (the hook handlers). The `plugins` array in `objectstack.json` holds plain descriptors (`{ name, version, dependencies, options }`), not anything that can be started.
3. Boot EE 18.6.0 with `OS_COMPOSED_ARTIFACT_URL=file:///…/dist/objectstack.json`. The plugin table shows 57 plugins and none of the six: no `com.objectstack.service.knowledge`, no app plugins, no connectors. No warning at build or at boot.
4. Consequence for this app: the knowledge service, the vector adapter and the clause index never exist. Everything that depends on them fails later and elsewhere (empty retrieval, hooks finding no service).

## Why (origin/main e9fa6b5d06)

- `packages/runtime/src/load-artifact-bundle.ts:199` `mergeRuntimeModule` imports the runtime module and reads `mod.functions ?? mod.default?.functions` only (L205). Plugins are never read from it.
- `packages/cli/src/utils/build-runtime.ts:233` bundles with `packages: 'external'`. Even if plugins were exported, their imports stay bare. In the EE 18.6.0 image `@objectstack/service-knowledge`, `@objectstack/embedder-openai` and `pg` do not resolve (`require.resolve` from `/repo/cloud/apps/objectos-ee` fails for all three), so a deployed artifact has no way to load them.

## The contract it breaks

- cloud `apps/objectos-ee/deploy/artifact-pinned-boot.md`, "What this mode does and does not mount": "The app's own plugins, flows and triggers come from the artifact".
- The build summary's `Runtime: 6 plugins` tells the author the plugins are in the build.

## Expected

One of these, decided by the maintainer:

- **Carry them.** The artifact ships the app's code plugins in a form the runtime can start (exported from the runtime module), together with their dependencies (bundled, or installed beside the artifact), and the loader mounts them.
- **Refuse them.** If code plugins are not supported on the artifact path, `os build` (or the boot) fails or warns loudly, naming each plugin that will not mount and saying what to do instead. Today the drop is silent.

## Workaround used to finish the evaluation

A derived image on top of `objectos-ee:18.6.0`: the app's production dependencies installed under `/srv/brightrule/node_modules`, and an entry `objectstack.config.ts` that imports the stock EE config unchanged and appends the app's plugins. With it the plugins mount (60 plugins) and the pgvector index is built. Every customer with a plugin-bearing app would have to maintain such an image per EE release.

Related (filed together):
- objectstack-ai/cloud#4935 — `ask` never loads a package's `surface: 'ask'` skill
- objectstack-ai/cloud#4933 — `search_knowledge` is never registered
- objectstack-ai/cloud#4934 — `query_data` fails on DeepSeek (`json_schema` response format)
